summary: Hugh B. Urban works in religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (circa 1992–1998) under Wendy Doniger, Bruce Lincoln, and Tony K. Stewart. Around 1998, he became an associate professor at Ohio State University.

Hugh Edward Richardson specialized in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Keble College (circa 1923–1927) and served in the Indian Civil Service (circa 1930–1950). He also founded the Tibet Society and the Institute of Tibetan Studies, Tring.

Hugh Gray was a scholar in Indology and other fields who studied at Battersea Grammar School. Around 1960 to 1983, he held posts at SOAS University of London and served as a lecturer at the University of London.

Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who earned his doctorate at Stanford University (circa 1968–1973). In 1974, he became a professor at Stony Brook University, and he served as executive director of the International Association for Philosophy and Literature (circa 1976–2013).

Hugo David is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études by 2012, held a fellowship at the University of Cambridge (2013–2014), and became a permanent member at École Française d'Extrême-Orient in 2015.
Hugo Makibi Enomiya-Lassalle was a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Yamada Koun circa 1962–1989 and held a post at Sophia University.
Hui-tzu Lu is a scholar in sinology and history and archaeology. Lu studied under teacher Jing-shen Tao, as well as under traditional teachers Zhiru Shi and Zhihui Shi, both attested in 2003.
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yi-hsun Huang, attested in 2011.
Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a student under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007) and held an academic post at the University of Hong Kong.

Huimin works in Buddhist studies and studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1986–1992). He held posts at Taipei National University of the Arts, the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and served as president of Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (circa 2014–2022).
Huishan Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Kuo-wei Liu. Lin also studied under Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.
Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under supervisor Kirill Solonin and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. Zhang held a lecturer post at Dongguk University, attested in 1996.

Humberto Maturana was a philosopher and biologist who studied at the University of Chile, University College London, and Harvard University (PhD 1956–1958). He held posts at MIT, University of Chile, and UIUC, and founded the Instituto Matríztica in 2000.
Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under doctoral supervisor Mark Allon.

Huston Smith was a philosopher of religion who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago in 1945. He held professorships at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1958–1973) and Syracuse University (1973–1983), and was a visiting professor at UC Berkeley (circa 1990–1999).

Huynh Kim Lan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under thesis advisers Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong (attested 2010).
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kapila Abhayawansa and earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, attested in 2015.

Hyakudai Sakamoto was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1948–1951). He held positions at the Tokyo University of Pharmacy and Life Sciences, Aoyama Gakuin University (circa 1968–1996), and the Open University of Japan (circa 1996–2002).

Hyejeong Choi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington (attested 2015). Choi has served as a visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara.
